data.title: HFCL boosts optical fibre capacity with ₹1,800 crore expansion drive
data.description:
HFCL Limited ( (IN:HFCL) ) has issued an update.

HFCL Limited’s board has approved an additional investment of about ₹820 crore to expand its optical fibre, optical fibre cable and preform manufacturing capacities, taking total planned capex for these projects to roughly ₹1,800 crore. The expansions will lift annual capacities to 43.10 million fibre kilometres for optical fibre, 62.00 million fibre kilometres for optical fibre cable and 600 MT for preform, with completion targeted between July and October 2028.

The company aims to build a more integrated and resilient optical fibre manufacturing platform spanning preform to connectivity solutions, aligning expanded capacity with a strong order book and robust business pipeline. HFCL expects the larger footprint to reinforce its position as a leading integrated optical communications player and enable it to capture rising global demand driven by AI, data centres, cloud, telecom network modernisation and fibre-led broadband roll-outs.

data.title: Aurora Cannabis Urges Shareholders to Reject Curaleaf’s Undervalued Hostile Bid
data.description:
Aurora Cannabis ( (TSE:ACB) ) has issued an announcement.

On Sept. 14, 2026, Aurora Cannabis publicly rejected Curaleaf Holdings’ application to halt its at-the-market equity program, characterizing the move as a distraction from Curaleaf’s hostile takeover bid, which Aurora says significantly undervalues the company. Aurora emphasized that the ATM program was disclosed in February 2026, has been largely inactive in recent weeks and is a long-term capital tool used to fund accretive growth initiatives, including recent UK acquisitions.

Aurora contrasted its debt-free status and strong cash position with Curaleaf’s more than $1 billion in debt, including $500 million of senior secured notes at an 11.5% interest rate, arguing that Curaleaf’s capital structure exposes shareholders to financial and dilution risks. The board and special committee have unanimously urged investors to reject the hostile offer, to withdraw any tendered shares, and to weigh the regulatory and governance concerns Aurora has raised about Curaleaf’s bid when considering the future value of their holdings.

data.title: Obsidian Energy Trims 2026 Output Guidance but Accelerates Peace River Growth Plan
data.description:
Obsidian Energy ( (TSE:OBE) ) has provided an announcement.

Obsidian Energy Ltd. is a Calgary-based upstream oil and gas producer listed on the TSX and NYSE American, with a portfolio of heavy oil assets in Peace River and light oil assets in areas such as Willesden Green, Crimson and Open Creek. The company focuses on development and waterflood-enhanced recovery in formations including Clearwater, Bluesky, Belly River and Cardium to drive liquids-weighted production growth in Western Canada.

Obsidian Energy announced on September 14, 2026, that it has updated its second-half capital program and revised its 2026 production guidance to 28,500–29,500 boe/d from 29,000–31,000 boe/d, citing wet-weather delays and compressor-driven downtime at its recently acquired Belly River assets, which are now back to about 2,400 boe/d. While capital spending remains in the C$300–325 million range and net debt guidance has edged up to about C$400 million, the company is accelerating Peace River development with new waterflood infrastructure and all-season roads, sustaining active drilling in its light oil portfolio, and reaffirming plans for more than 15% year-over-year production growth in 2027, underscoring a strategy focused on operational resilience and longer-term output expansion despite near-term production headwinds.

data.title: Stewards Inc Updates Preferred Stock Conversion Ownership Limits
data.description:
Stewards Inc ( (SWRD) ) just unveiled an announcement.

On September 9, 2026, Stewards, Inc.’s board and all holders of its 71,250,000 outstanding Series A Preferred shares approved an amendment to the Certificate of Designation governing that class of stock. The change, made effective upon filing with the Nevada Secretary of State on September 10, 2026, replaces a 9.99% cap on the Maximum Percentage of common stock ownership upon conversion with a 100% threshold and removes the prior mechanism for holders to adjust that cap by notice.

The amendment leaves all other economic and voting terms of the Series A Preferred Stock unchanged, including conversion rate, timing, dividends, redemption, liquidation, and voting rights. By eliminating the ownership cap while preserving the requirement that Section 3(e) cannot be waived without consent from a majority of common shareholders, the move potentially increases flexibility for preferred holders to convert into common shares while maintaining a safeguard for existing common equity investors.

data.title: REMOR SOLAR POLSKA Appeals Court Order in Advisory Fee Dispute
data.description:

REMOR SOLAR POLSKA SA has filed an appeal against a judgment by the District Court in Szczecin ordering it to pay Delta Capital Group over PLN 380,000 plus interest and nearly PLN 30,000 in litigation costs. The dispute stems from a 2021 advisory agreement under which Delta Capital Group supported REMOR SOLAR in obtaining external financing that led to an investment deal with Atlas Energy Polska.

The company maintains that the advisory fee was only partially due, reflecting the actual level of financing obtained, and it disagrees with the court’s first-instance decision. By appealing, REMOR SOLAR seeks a complete dismissal of Delta Capital Group’s claim, highlighting ongoing legal uncertainty around its advisory obligations that could have financial and reputational implications for stakeholders until the case becomes final.

data.title: MeglioQuesto Moves Forward on Restructuring as Borgosesia Bid Stands
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Meglioquesto S.P.A. ( (IT:MQSPA) ).

MeglioQuesto S.p.A. has reported that, following the Court of Milan’s deadline in the simplified composition with creditors procedures of several subsidiaries, no competing bids were submitted to improve the acquisition offer made by Gruppo Borgosesia. This closes the competitive phase of the financial and industrial restructuring plan, which envisages Borgosesia acquiring the subsidiaries’ businesses and transferring them to MeglioQuesto as part of a broader capital strengthening transaction.

The restructuring transaction can only be completed once the competent bodies authorize it, with potential acceleration if an application under the Business Crisis and Insolvency Code is approved at a hearing scheduled for 19 November. The outcome of this process is expected to be significant for MeglioQuesto’s financial stability and operational consolidation, and the company has committed to promptly updating the market on any authorizations and resulting measures.
